name: policy-dev
description: Guided setup for one policy-development run: task, optional demonstration, Synthesizer only or Synthesizer + Adversary, budgets and retries, Adversary sampling strategy, then an explicit confirmation. Plain data: any agent (Muse Wonder, Muse Code, a person) can read the questions, and the Studio server walks them as a state machine without a model call. Muse tokens cost about $13.5 per million, so nothing launches without an explicit 'yes' at the last step, and 'go with defaults' never skips that step.

steps.default: put the bowl on the plate
steps.ask: What should the robot do? Describe the task in one sentence.
Do you have an example demonstration?

choices.label: video
choices.help: attach a human demo video with the + button

choices.label: demospec
choices.help: use a DemoSpec already extracted under data/demospecs/

choices.label: none
choices.help: no demonstration: the generator works from the task text only

steps.ask: Attach the video with the + button (mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi, m4v; up to 200 MB). Say 'skip' to continue without it.
Which DemoSpec? Give its number or file name.

choices.label: synthesizer
choices.help: write the first program from the demo and task, then stop

choices.label: synthesizer + adversary
choices.help: write the program, then run the closed loop: attack, repair, gate

steps.ask: Synthesizer token budget (hard cap on new Muse tokens)?
Synthesizer max retries (repair attempts on a failing program)?
Adversary budget: how many attacks (cycles) at most?
Adversary max retries: how many stalled cycles on one failure before escalating to you?
How should the Adversary pick what to attack?

choices.label: thompson
choices.help: adaptive: favour categories most likely to break the policy (eta 0.2)

choices.label: random
choices.help: uniform sampling over categories (eta 1.0), the baseline
